manifest_schema.title: PolicyManifest
manifest_schema.description: Top-level policy manifest — the YAML file that users write.

auth_providers.description: Cloud auth provider configurations for IAM-mapped role awareness.

default_owner.description: Default owner for ALTER DEFAULT PRIVILEGES (e.g. "app_owner").

profiles.description:
Reusable privilege profiles. Stored as a `BTreeMap` so YAML
serialization is deterministic — two `pgroles generate` runs against
the same database produce byte-identical output.

retirements.description: Explicit role-retirement workflows for roles that should be removed.

role_pattern.description: Default role naming pattern for schema profile bindings.

schemas.description: Schema bindings that expand profiles into concrete roles/grants.

AuthProvider.description:
Cloud authentication provider configuration.

Declares awareness of cloud IAM-mapped roles so pgroles can correctly
reference auto-created role names in grants and memberships.

oneOf.description:
Google Cloud SQL IAM authentication.
Service accounts map to PG roles like `user@project.iam`.

Google AlloyDB IAM authentication.
IAM users and groups map to PostgreSQL roles managed by AlloyDB.

AWS RDS IAM authentication.
IAM users authenticate via token; the PG role must have `rds_iam` granted.
Azure Entra ID (AAD) authentication for Azure Database for PostgreSQL.

ConfigValue.description:
A role configuration parameter value.

Values are always strings — quote numbers and booleans (e.g.
`statement_timeout: "30000"`, `jit: "off"`). The Kubernetes CRD schema
types config values as strings, and the CLI enforces the same rule so a
manifest means the same thing whether it is applied with `pgroles` or
`kubectl`. PostgreSQL coerces the string to the parameter's type.

DefaultPrivilege.description:
Default privilege configuration.

The scope rules are also expressed as CEL so the API server rejects a bad
entry at apply time. `resolved_scope` enforces the same rules for the CLI,
which has no admission step.

grant.description: Grantee, privileges, and future object kind to reconcile.

owner.description: The role that owns newly created objects. If omitted, uses manifest's default_owner.

schema.description:
Schema shorthand, equivalent to `scope: {type: schema, schema: ...}`.
Exactly one of `schema` and `scope` must be set.

scope.description:
Where the defaults apply: one schema, or owner-wide (global). Global
scope renders `ALTER DEFAULT PRIVILEGES` without an `IN SCHEMA` clause.

x-kubernetes-validations.message: exactly one of `schema` and `scope` must be set

DefaultPrivilegeGrant.description: A single default privilege grant entry.

ensure.description: Desired privilege state: present grants it; absent explicitly revokes it.

on_type.description: Kind of future object affected by the default privilege.

privileges.description: PostgreSQL privileges to reconcile on the selected objects.

role.description:
The role receiving the default privilege. Only used in top-level default_privileges
(in profiles, the role is determined by expansion). The exact-uppercase
value `PUBLIC` means the PostgreSQL PUBLIC pseudo-role.

DefaultPrivilegeScopeSpec.description: Scope selector for a default-privileges entry.

schema.description: Schema name. Required for `type: schema`, forbidden for `type: global`.

type.description: Global or per-schema scope of the default privilege.

x-kubernetes-validations.message: `schema` is required when type is `schema` and forbidden when type is `global`

Ensure.description:
Whether the listed privileges must exist or must not exist.

`absent` asserts one ACL edge only. It plans a REVOKE when the privilege is
found live, and it says nothing about access the grantee may still have
through role membership or ownership.

Grant.description: A concrete grant on a specific object or wildcard.

ensure.description: Desired object privilege state: present grants it; absent explicitly revokes it.

object.description: Object kind and target to which the privileges apply.

privileges.description: PostgreSQL privileges to reconcile on the selected objects.

role.description:
The grantee. The exact-uppercase value `PUBLIC` means the PostgreSQL
PUBLIC pseudo-role; any other value is an ordinary role name.

MemberSpec.description:
A single member of a role.

Both `inherit` and `admin` are optional. When omitted, they default to
`inherit: true` and `admin: false` at resolution time (in `RoleGraph`
construction). Keeping them optional in the CRD avoids Kubernetes
injecting default values into the stored resource, which causes
perpetual diffs in GitOps tools like ArgoCD.

admin.description: Whether the member can administer the role. Defaults to `false`.

inherit.description: Whether the member inherits the role's privileges. Defaults to `true`.

Membership.description: A membership declaration — which members belong to a role.

exclusive.description:
Assert that `members` is the complete membership of `role`: plan a
REVOKE for any live member not listed here. Only meaningful for
predefined (`pg_*`) and `external: true` roles, whose undeclared
members are otherwise left untouched — memberships of ordinary managed
roles are already reconciled exhaustively. Defaults to `false` so that
adopting pgroles never strips provider-granted memberships (for
example `pg_monitor` grants made by a cloud platform) without an
explicit assertion.

members.description: Roles that should receive this membership.

role.description: PostgreSQL role granted to the listed members.

name.description:
Object name, or "*" for all objects. Omit for schema-level grants;
required for database grants, where it names the connected database.

schema.description: Schema name. Required for most object types except database.

ObjectType.description: PostgreSQL object types that can have privileges granted on them.

PasswordSource.description:
Source for a role password. Passwords are never stored in YAML manifests.

This follows the same security model as `DATABASE_URL` — secrets come from
the runtime environment, not from configuration files.

from_env.description: Name of the environment variable containing the password.

Profile.description: A reusable privilege profile — defines what grants a role should have.

config.description:
Role-level configuration parameter defaults for generated roles,
applied via `ALTER ROLE ... SET parameter = value`. Values support the
`{schema}` and `{profile}` placeholders (the same two `role_pattern`
supports), substituted per `schema x profile` expansion — e.g.
`search_path: "{schema}"` becomes `search_path: inventory` on the role
generated for the `inventory` schema. Keys are literal PostgreSQL
parameter names; placeholders are not substituted in keys (a `{schema}`
key is rejected by [`is_valid_config_parameter_name`], same as any
other invalid parameter name). Values are always strings — see
[`ConfigValue`].

default_privileges.description: Privileges to grant on future objects created by the configured owner.

grants.description: Object privilege templates expanded for each bound schema.

inherit.description: Whether privileges from role memberships are inherited automatically.

login.description: Whether the role may initiate database sessions.

ProfileGrant.description: A grant template within a profile (schema is filled in during expansion).

ensure.description:
Whether the privilege must be present or absent. Expansion rejects
`absent`, because a profile is an additive template. The field exists
so that rejection can name the offending profile, instead of the value
being dropped as an unknown key and the grant expanding to its
opposite.

object.description: Object kind and target to which the privileges apply.

privileges.description: PostgreSQL privileges to reconcile on the selected objects.

ProfileObjectTarget.description: Object target within a profile — schema is omitted (filled during expansion).

name.description: Object name, or "*" for all objects of this type. Omit for schema-level grants.

bypassrls.description: Whether the role bypasses row-level security.

config.description:
Role-level configuration parameter defaults, applied via
`ALTER ROLE ... SET parameter = value`. Keys are PostgreSQL setting
names (e.g. `role`, `search_path`, `statement_timeout`); values are
applied as string literals. Settings present on the role in the
database but absent here are `RESET` in authoritative mode.

connection_limit.description: Maximum concurrent connections for the role; -1 means unlimited.

createdb.description: Whether the role may create databases.

createrole.description: Whether the role may create and administer roles, subject to server-version rules.

external.description:
Treat this role as managed by another system. pgroles may reference it
in grants, ownership, and memberships, but will not create, alter, drop,
password-manage, or manage memberships granted from this role.

inherit.description: Whether privileges from role memberships are inherited automatically.

login.description: Whether the role may initiate database sessions.

password.description:
Password source for this role. Passwords are never stored in the manifest
directly — only a reference to an environment variable is allowed.

password_valid_until.description:
Password expiration timestamp (ISO 8601, e.g. "2025-12-31T00:00:00Z").
Maps to PostgreSQL's `VALID UNTIL` clause.

preserve_undeclared_grants.description:
Preserve this role's undeclared in-scope object grants during
convergence. Revokes against the role are skipped unless the revoked
privileges are explicitly asserted absent (`ensure: absent`), so a
brownfield role can be brought under pgroles management before its
full grant surface is declared. Declared grants still converge and
owner-inherent privileges are unaffected.

replication.description: Whether the role may initiate replication connections.

superuser.description: Whether the role bypasses PostgreSQL permission checks as a superuser.

RoleRetirement.description: Declarative workflow for retiring an existing role.

drop_owned.description: Whether to run `DROP OWNED BY` before dropping the role.

reassign_owned_to.description: Optional successor role for `REASSIGN OWNED BY ... TO ...`.

role.description: The role to retire and ultimately drop.

terminate_sessions.description: Whether to terminate other active sessions for the role before drop.

SchemaBinding.description: Associates a PostgreSQL schema with one or more reusable privilege profiles.

owner.description: Override default_owner for this schema's default privileges.

profiles.description: Profile names to expand for this schema.

role_pattern.description:
Role naming pattern. Supports `{schema}` and `{profile}` placeholders.
Overrides the policy pattern; otherwise inherits it, falling back to `"{schema}-{profile}"`.
